observations: The page number «74» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. The page has no signature. L01 continues the sentence that ends p. 73 (JP2 0105, L36), «Batt. hat solche Tafeln für die Breiten». L02: «13h», «16h», «15m», the letters raised. N01-N02: «Ibid.», al-Battānī in Nallino's edition (p. 73, N02).

A figure stands at the left of L08-L22, which are set in a narrower measure at its right; it is not reproduced. A circle (the meridian) with Z at the top, P at the upper right, A and E at the upper left, H and T at the ends of a horizontal dashed diameter, K and Q at the lower right; dashed lines from the centre to Z, P, A, E, K and Q. Within the circle the arcs of the horizon from H through D and L to T, of the equator from A through the vernal point, D and N to Q, of the ecliptic from E through the vernal point and L to K, and of the circle of declination from P through L to N; the angle at D marked with a small arc. The vernal point is labelled with a small sign like a γ, where the text has ♈; the other letters are italic.

L05-L27. Checked: in the triangle D N L, right-angled at N, with the angle D between the equator and the horizon equal to the altitude of the equator, 90° − φ (the arc A H of the meridian), and the side L N the declination δ, the rule sin a = tg b : tg B of p. 72 (JP2 0104, L10) gives sin DN = tg δ : tg (90° − φ) = tg δ · tg φ; the point D of the equator rises with L, so that ♈D, the oblique ascension, is ♈N less DN for a northern declination and ♈N plus DN for a southern one; tg δ · tg φ = sin φ sin δ : (cos φ cos δ), al-Battānī's form (L27).

The formulas: L05 and L24 italic but for «für die Breite», the signs and the brackets, L05 with the sign ∓ (minus above plus); L16, L22 and L23 displayed; L16, L23 and L24 have the minus as a long dash, in L16 and L24 printed in two pieces (13 and 31 px, 23 and 20 px, with gaps of 2 and 3 px); L20 and L22 «90°—φ», «(90—φ)», the long dash set close. The fractions of L21, L22 and L27 are built up, written {fr:NUMERATOR|DENOMINATOR}; in L21 the formula stands within large round brackets that span the fraction, the colon set close after the bracket; L22 ends with a comma after a small space. «∠», the angle sign of L20, an upright ∠, where p. 44 (JP2 0076) has ∢; «♈», the sign of the vernal point (L10, L13, L16, L23), upright.

L13-L14: «die Ascensio obliqua» upright, divided «Ascen-|sio», where L05-L06, L24 and L32 set it in italics; L15 «Ascensional-Differenz.» in italics. L08: «Menelaus» spaced. L34: «im 1.° des Widders (eigentlich 0.°)», the degree sign after the point of the ordinal. The rule of L32-L34 continues on p. 75.

Spaced type, marked {sp:}: «Batt.», «Kh.», «Ptol.», «Menelaus», «Heiberg», «Manitius»; italics: the names of places in L01, «Ascensio obliqua», «Ascensio recta», «Ascensional-Differenz.», the letters of the figure and the formulas, «Sūrya-Siddhānta». The dashes of N01-N03 are the long dash of the small type (32-34 px; in N03 printed in two pieces, 8 and 24 px).
The colons and semicolons stand after the thin space of the edition (9-13 px measured).
